lesson: Today we work on one technique, starting a poem in the middle of things, with no explanation of who or where you are. The poem drops you straight into a moment already going. Look at the first words, wood smoke, first of the year, threading in cold. No name, no scene set up, no one morning I woke and smelled smoke. It just gives you the smell. Then the floors a shock against your souls. Then there's a list you made past dark. You get facts as they land, not an introduction. This works in a plain way. Because nothing is explained, you fill in the situation yourself while you read. That makes you pay attention. You are working to keep up, so you stay inside the poem. Try this. Cut your first two lines of setup, and begin with the first thing the person sees, hears or smells. The second time through, notice how fast you know where you are, even with no one explaining it.
